claims.claim: Reviewers report technical issues launching or running the game on PC, specifically mentioning problems with AMD and NVIDIA hardware combinations that require external fixes or workarounds.

citations.review_text:
Requires an unofficial fix from GitHub to run if you have an AMD CPU + NVIDIA GPU combo.
Dialogue is also total cheeks and physically painful to listen to so far from the little I've played. Might update if I keep playing.

I’ve spent more than an hour trying to get this game to run, and the “fix” ended up being plugging my HDMI cable into the motherboard instead of my GPU. Absolute clown show.

The internet told me to disable my dedicated graphics card in Device Manager, start the game, then enable it again afterwards. Sounds simple, right? Wrong. The intro logos are apparently tied to FPS, so I had to sit through these stupid Bethesda logos at literally 1 FPS for like five minutes straight.

Then, the moment I re-enabled my GPU, the game crashed. G ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ G.

After that, Reddit geniuses started saying it’s because AMD CPUs and NVIDIA GPUs are somehow incompatible or whatever. So I deleted a bunch of software, installed different drivers, tried every dumb “solution” people posted online, nothing worked.

And after all that, the actual fix was just plugging the HDMI cable into the motherboard. Either I somehow got a one-in-a-million bug, or every Bethesda player secretly runs their monitor through the motherboard by default. Who knows.

Suck my balls, Bethesda.

If you have any type of AMD hardware, you will need to update files from github because an outdated dll file will not allow the game to launch. On top of that the games borderless / windowed mode are not coded correctly and won't allow proper tabbing out of the game. If you tab out via steam overlay the game will become incredibly slow and require a relaunch. 

Play this anywhere but PC.
insanely buggy and hard to launch on AMD + Nvidia pair

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game suffers from poor PC optimization and technical issues such as frame rate drops, screen tearing, and stuttering.

citations.review_text: the game had some screen tearing, render and blur issues but after months of not playing, i played it at last again and it definitely is a great game. Had to tweak out some settings for it to be actually viewable.
the game runs really bad on my system. it's a shame.

Phenomenal game, which is especially noteworthy given the act it follows after the near perfect first game. Good story, excellent gameplay, unique art style, and some good replay value to boot with two fully voiced main characters that have different mechanics each, requiring one playthrough with each of them to truly get the full experience. Only downside is that this game is quite poorly optimized for PC, but as long as you don't mind lowering your resolution/graphics quality a little bit you can still maintain consistently good framerates while preserving the unique art style the game intends.

I really enjoyed the Dishonored series, although I still haven’t finished Death of the Outsider.

The first game remains my favorite. Of course, that’s a matter of personal taste, but the Victorian-inspired British architecture is far more aesthetically pleasing to me, and I also find the original game much darker in tone. That said, I have to admit that moving the sequel to a new setting was the right decision. The world feels vibrant, believable, and full of life.

Just as he did with Half-Life 2, Viktor Antonov created a truly memorable visual identity for Dishonored. The game also contains a few stylistic nods to Half-Life: some architectural elements resemble the industrial aesthetic of City 17, while the Tallboy is hard not to compare to the Strider.

From a gameplay perspective, Dishonored 2 is a much bigger game. The levels are larger, you can now knock enemies unconscious from above, and the overall playtime has increased thanks to the option of completing the game as either of the two protagonists. The story is solid as well.

There were, however, a couple of issues that I encountered during my playthrough: the audio and the optimization. I honestly couldn’t figure out what was wrong with the sound. Whenever I turned the camera away, conversations would become significantly quieter or disappear altogether. I checked both the in-game and Windows audio settings but couldn’t find a solution. Could this be related to the FOV?

The optimization was disappointing too. Even on High and Ultra settings, the game wasn’t delivering the frame rates I expected from a 2016 title running on my hardware.

Is it still worth buying today? Absolutely. Dishonored 2 is one of the most stylish immersive sims I’ve ever played.

i wish i could recommend this game, the level design seems pretty good, but the game is 10 years old and for some reason i can't get it to run no matter how many settings i change in game and in the rest of my pc, it's insulting that a 10 year old game is so unoptimized that modern hardware is still having issues with it, whenever i move the camera it feels as if i'm playing at less than 30 fps, regardless of what the steam fps counter says, if i somehow manage to make it run properly i will update this review, but in the meantime, ♥♥♥♥ this game

citations.review_text:
The first Dishonored is one of the best stealth games i ever played so i wanted to try the second one. I bought this game after seeing the gameplay, the new story with two playable protagonists and ofc new powers and weapons. 
But after buying and instaling the game the game cannot launch. This game has a problem where if you have a modern pc with an AMD and an Nvidia grafics card combined the game will not launch and you cant play the game. I can only play Dishonored 2 if i turn off my Nvidia card. Then if i play the game i only get like 5-18 FPS at the lowest settings. Unplayable. Solving this problem means that i have to buy a new PC or go on some sketchy website to fix the games code. I tried many things to fix this and nothing works. At the end i removed the game from my library. Beacause this game is almost 11 years old i dont think that this problem will be patched in an update soon. I also saw that Dishonored: Death of the Outsider has the same exect problem as this game. If i didnt have this problem i think that the game would be amazing.  Still Recomended for those who can play it.

8/10
game dont launch anymore but the original does
Game doesn't start anymore. Instantly closed on start.

Edited: Game won't launch if you have AMD CPU + NVIDIA GPU. While I'm aware of a user made fix, the company should issue a fix for it. Using this combination of components is very common and it affects a lot of people. This shouldn't be ignored by them.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the story and writing are weaker and less immersive compared to the first game.

citations.review_text: Fantastic improvements to the gameplay as compared to the original, but with a weaker story.

gameplay is an improvement over the first game, otherwise a step down in story, immersion, and other areas from the first game. Main villain is lame and so are most of the other villains. Still worth a buy if you get it on sale.

Seven hours in and the verdict is already clear: Dishonored 2 is a competent sequel that understands what made the original work, then second-guesses itself at every turn and adds 40% more stuff that dilutes rather than improves. It's still good — atmosphere and world-building remain exceptional — but it's proof that bigger doesn't mean better, especially when the original nailed something most games never figure out.

The level design is technically accomplished (Clockwork Mansion is genuinely clever), but it lacks the elegant simplicity that made the first game's spaces sing. The original trusted players to improvise; Dishonored 2 feels like it's anxiously showing off every puzzle solution, every alternate route, every way a level could be approached instead of letting discovery happen organically. The magic abilities are expanded (which sounds great until you realize the original's focused arsenal was actually the smarter design choice), and the new protagonist Emily adds mechanics that don't meaningfully improve on Corvo's approach — they just add options.

The atmosphere is still there — Karnaca's seaside decay, the political intrigue, the sense of a world operating independently of your actions. The problem is the game keeps telling that atmosphere instead of letting it breathe. Cutscenes interrupt flow, exposition dumps interrupt immersion, the story feels bloated compared to the original's lean revenge tale.

It's not bad. It's just a sequel that mistook "more" for "better," then forgot that the original's brilliance came from restraint. The first Dishonored proved that elegance beats ambition.

Still worth playing if the first connected with you. Just manage expectations — this is a solid follow-up to a masterpiece, not a masterpiece itself.

Великолепный иммерсив сим, настоящий уровень мастерства Arkane.
Я пришёл в игру с сомнениями насчет стелса, но она показала, что хороший стелс - это не ожидание в кустах, а поиск решений.
Сюжет слабее первой части - злодеи уже не вызывают того чувства гнили и ненависти, но игру прекрасно вытянул геймплей. В итоге я не уничтожил врагов, я просто забрал у них власть и оставил им последствия их собственных решений. Одна из лучших игр в жанре.
Not as good as the first game in terms of story, but still great in gameplay

Okay so compared to the first game gameplay,scenery and graphics wise it's better in every way, way more stuff to do the city is more alive and the idea that you can play with emily or corvo is a great idea which changes dialogue and interactions with old and new characters, the premise is similar with a few differences which idk man a little more creativity was needed on that part, now for the missions i can say they are interesting and fun with the classic "do what you want to get to your goal" just like the first game. my only problem is that the game is too bright and happy compared to the first one. the whole point of the first game is that the kingdom was taken over by a dictator and the plague roaming the streets, in the second game except from the last mission which is pretty gloomy, the new location is very bright even if there is also a dictator that is basically sucking the wealth from that city which artistically doesn't make sense to me. but it's still a great game,i loved it and the new things it brought and it was quite a ride i loved watching the ending

It's good if you have leftover goodwill from the first one, worldbuilding feels wider than deep though. The Heart in the first one told you about the goings on of specific districts and the histories of specific buildings, this time it just kinda tells you "there's a class divide" in 50 different ways. First game gave you enough lore on just the sewers to write a textbook. This one, not so much. Also not buying that the Outsider from this game and the last game are the same guy, they had him show his hand too much. They completely changed where they do and don't show restraint in the worldbuilding in a way that meaningfully changes the character of the world.

The levels too. Sokolov's lab in the first game felt like a real place, for example. It was just a building that had Sokolov's research and stuff in it. Jindosh's clockwork mansion, it's fun, but I don't buy that it plausibly exists in the same way. The logistics there don't work. His work is repeatedly shown to have replicability issues because other people can't even take it apart and put it back together, the mansion runs on it, have you tried building a mansion as just one guy? I just don't buy it. it's a gameplay setpiece that exists as a gameplay setpiece. I'm just not convinced, it stretches my suspension of disbelief too far, like it breaks the very rules it establishes.

The coup in the first one felt real too, this time it just feels like a witch (who is a bit "somehow Palpatine returned") came in and made it happen.  That's another example.

Gameplay is fun though.

I'm glad to say that this game runs smoothly on my PC handheld. All my gripes come from the gameplay. I'm a stealth game fan even though I'm not great at them. Stealth in this game is highly encouraged. I really tried to approach it as a stealth player but the problem is that the stealth aspect simply isn't that fun. I couldn't really find that many tactics in the game to use stealth. The best way to deal with enemies is to simply find different routes around them to where you're no longer interacting with them. For the portion I've played this game takes place primarily in the middle of the day with fully lit areas. There are barely any shadows to hide in. Going full on Rambo is much more enjoyable yet it doesn't save the game's lackluster gameplay. The violence is needlessly gratuitous and doesn't match the character motivations. I love me some gore but coming up to a person to do a stealth kill you'd think it'd be less of a blood bath (limbs and heads being removed). The story is very basic. World-building is like a dull alternate copy of Bioshock. There are a ton of collectibles to encourage level exploration, yet all of the items are dull "read-me" content. If you don't explore you won't be able to fully upgrade your character.

RECOMMENDED

Dishonored 2 is proof that Arkane Studios understands immersive sims better than anyone else. 

Karnaca is an incredible setting—dense, vertical, and brimming with atmosphere. But what makes the game truly extraordinary is how much freedom it gives you. Playing as Emily with her new supernatural abilities (Domino is easily one of the most satisfying mechanics in any stealth game) completely changes how you navigate encounters. 

Special mention has to go to "The Clockwork Mansion" and "A Crack in the Slab"—two levels that push the boundaries of spatial puzzle design and time manipulation. The game never holds your hand, rewards exploration around every corner, and gives you complete agency over how high or low your chaos gets.

If you have any love for stealth, creative combat, or level design, this is an absolute 10/10 masterpiece.

I take this/these games with a grain of salt. Gameplaywise, they are a great stealth (or not stealth) games as you have the option to play sneaky or not, play without killing people, or go full maniac, which will all influence the story. The story is also interesting and well written. These games are generally fun to play.

NOW the BIG BUT... this game has several tiny and some VEEEEEERY BIG ISSUE: tiny problems are some bugs, which sometimes just get on your nerves BUT also these bugs occasionaly ruin your progress especially when you are trying to play the sneaky no kill route.
Random people die, which makes it so hard and incredibly frustrating to get the "Clean Hands" (aka never killed anyone) Achievement. One of the most boring games I've played and I've played quite a few.

To start with, there is basically no reason to play it stealthily and with no deaths, since it doesn't reward the player for being cautious. On the contrary, it punishes every little mistake you make. The maps are quite large and are comprised of several multi-level labyrinth-styled locations (flats, offices, building, etc). To navigate those safely you need the x-ray vision, which has been nerfed here quite dramatically in both range and visibility in comparison to the original. There hundreds of enemies in each location and each and every one of them moves randomly through locations, has keen perception and are extremely vigilant, while you do not have much of anything to help you 1. gather every collectible 2. complete the level stealthily. You can always get things done and get out, but you will be leaving everything behind.

You can, however, not do any of those things, but then you won't get the gratification of a proper ending. The combat system is just as broken as it was in the original with pistol dominating every enemy in sight. 

Also, there are no incentives here. E.g., in RE4 after a high-intensity fight, challenging puzzle or location that is difficult to get across there is always the merchant. Seeing him is like a breath of fresh air. 
While there are merchants in this game, each one is different and none stood out, all seemed like generic NPCs with different pricing/ They are scattered randomly throughout the game too. Weapon upgrades are extremely limited and boring, so there are 0 reasons to collect coins and treasures. There are almost no side quest here as well. 

The game runs like crap 10 years after the release too.

Prepare to spam quick save/load if you want to beat the game the way it was intended.
